title: Presence
lead: Open hands, good posture, a real smile, the right voice, sincerity, and moving with grace.

read.where: An open hand says **“welcome”** before a word is spoken.

stops.name: Open hand service
stops.text: Gesture and present with an **open, relaxed palm**, never a **pointed finger**: toward the menu, a seat, the restroom, a dish. Keep **hands visible** and **out of pockets**.

stops.name: Posture
stops.text: Stand **tall** with shoulders relaxed and weight balanced. **Never lean** on chairs, side stands or tables. At the table, stay calm and still, hands relaxed, **bending slightly** to speak with seated guests without ever **hovering** over them.

keyPoints.line: the table’s energy: quiet or bright.

read.bigIdea: A real smile reaches the eyes.
read.where: Each guest deserves a **fresh, unhurried** version of you.

stops.name: Smiling
stops.text: A real smile **reaches the eyes**. Smile **as you approach**, **before you speak** and when you **say goodbye**. Between tables, **shake off any stress**.

stops.name: Vocal tone and pace
stops.text: Speak warmly, **a little lower and a touch slower** than ordinary conversation, and **match the table’s energy**: quiet for an intimate dinner, brighter for a celebration.

keyPoints.line: ask, listen, and use what you learn.

read.bigIdea: Noticing is where every great gesture begins.

stops.name: Sincerity
stops.text: Be **genuinely curious**, listen to the answers, and use what you learn. If you love a dish, **say why**. “I’m not sure, let me find out” **always beats a guess**.

stops.name: Moving with grace
stops.text: Walk with purpose: **never rush, never run**. Carry plates with **two hands** and a steady core, serve from the **guest’s side** without reaching across them, and **yield the aisle**. **Scan every table** on every pass; **never travel empty-handed**.

sources: Baldwin Restaurant Group, The Art of Table Service: 2 to 7.
